title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 8th District
area: Northeastern Minnesota, including Duluth, the Iron Range, and the Boundary Waters region.

context.text: Incumbent Pete Stauber (R) won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 86.4% of the vote against Anthony Hamilton. Trina Swanson won the Democratic primary with 76.8% against Luke Gulbranson and John Munter.

candidates.name: Pete Stauber
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 86.4% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2019); Chair, Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee

summary.text: Stauber is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 8th District, first elected in 2018. A former minor-league hockey player and Duluth police officer, he previously served on the Hermantown city council and the St. Louis County Board. He chairs the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the Committee on Natural Resources and also serves on the Committee on Small Business and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

background.text: Born in Duluth, Minnesota, in 1966; graduated from Denfeld High School in Duluth.

Earned a bachelor's degree in criminology from Lake Superior State University in 1986, where he played hockey and, according to his House website, was team captain of a Division I national championship team.
Signed with the Detroit Red Wings organization in 1990 and played in the American Hockey League and ECHL before retiring because of a neck injury.

Joined the Duluth Police Department in 1995 and served for more than two decades, rising to lieutenant, according to Wikipedia. His House website says he was shot in the head while off duty in 1995 and that his experiences as an officer shaped his view that more should be done to support law enforcement.
Served on the Hermantown city council (2001-2005 and 2011-2013) and on the St. Louis County Board of Commissioners (2013-2019).
Won the 2018 election for Minnesota's 8th District, defeating Democratic-Farmer-Labor nominee Joe Radinovich for the seat vacated by Rick Nolan, and took office in January 2019.
Chairs the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the Committee on Natural Resources, and serves on the Committee on Small Business and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.
Lives in Hermantown with his wife, Jodi, an Iraq War veteran, and their six children, according to his House website.

priorities.text: Chairs the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the Committee on Natural Resources, focused on mining and energy development in the Iron Range.
Serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Small Business, including the Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains subcommittee.

positions.summary: Opposed a Biden administration ban on offshore oil and gas drilling and pledged to fight restrictions on fossil fuel production.
positions.quote: We will use every tool in our toolbox to fight this ban and lead the world in energy production once again!

positions.summary: Introduced legislation to protect a Defense Department program that transfers surplus equipment to local police departments.
positions.quote: I will do everything in my power to ensure my brothers and sisters in the blue and brown receive the equipment they need to keep themselves and communities they serve safe.

positions.summary: Condemned a Minneapolis mayor's refusal to cooperate with ICE deportations of people in the country illegally, urging the city to prioritize cooperation with immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: we urge you to prioritize their needs over those of criminals and terrorists

record.text: Chairs the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the Committee on Natural Resources in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), a role he has held since the 118th Congress.

Serves on the Committee on Small Business (Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains subcommittee) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Served as ranking member of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee during the 117th Congress (2021-2022), before Republicans held the House majority.
Introduced the Lifesaving Gear for Police Act with Rep. Don Bacon to protect the Department of Defense's 1033 program that transfers surplus military equipment to local law enforcement.

candidates.name: Trina Swanson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 76.8% of the vote.

summary.text: Swanson is a former senior official at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) from Hermantown, running as the Democratic nominee (DFL) against incumbent Pete Stauber in her first campaign for public office. According to her campaign, she left federal service in 2025 and started a law firm before entering the race. She is campaigning on affordability, government accountability and rural community investment.

background.text: Grew up in Hermantown, Minnesota, and graduated from Hermantown High School; according to her campaign website, her mother was a nurse and her father worked in construction and at a paper mill.
Began her federal career at 18 at the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Duluth, working there through college and law school; she graduated from the Mitchell Hamline School of Law.

Joined USCIS after law school, first in the Minnesota field office, and held senior roles in Minneapolis, Washington, D.C., Germany and Kenya, including responsibilities during national emergency operations in the United States.
According to her campaign website, she rose to Director of International Operations at USCIS and received two DHS Secretary's Awards during about 25 years of federal service.
Says she left federal service in 2025 rather than compromise her oath after being asked to carry out directives she believed were unethical, then returned to Minnesota and started a law firm.
Announced her candidacy for Minnesota's 8th District in January 2026, won the DFL endorsement in April, and won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with about 77% of the vote.

priorities.text: Affordability: lowering prescription drug prices, expanding rural health care access, protecting Medicare and Social Security, and supporting jobs in mining, manufacturing, and the skilled trades.
priorities.quote: Affordability is my top priority. I will focus on lowering prescription drug prices, expanding rural health care access, protecting Medicare and Social Security, strengthening domestic supply chains, and supporting good-paying jobs in mining, manufacturing, and the skilled trades.

priorities.text: Government stability and accountability, including opposing stock ownership or trading by members of Congress.
priorities.quote: Congresspeople should not be allowed to hold or trade stock when in office.

priorities.text: Community presence, including in-person town halls in every county, infrastructure investment, and responsible mineral extraction that protects the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness.
priorities.quote: investing in infrastructure, supporting responsible extraction of critical minerals while protecting the environment, protecting the BWCA

positions.summary: Supports lowering prescription drug prices and expanding rural health care access.
positions.quote: I will focus on lowering prescription drug prices, expanding rural health care access, protecting Medicare and Social Security

positions.summary: Supports 'responsible immigration reform that protects our borders while upholding our values,' without specifying enforcement or deportation policy.
positions.quote: ensuring responsible immigration reform that protects our borders while upholding our values
